title: Alloy Enterprises Unveils 3D Printed Copper Cooling for AI Data Centers
summary: Boston-based Alloy Enterprises announced a line of copper direct liquid cooling (DLC) components for AI and HPC data centers, made with its proprietary Stack Forging process, which the article describes as born from additive manufacturing. The company states its single-piece copper cold plates have up to 10 times lower pressure drop than standard parts and can run on warmer water (around 44 °C). The company also states that cold plates can help data centers reduce total energy use by up to 23%, and that Alloy is already shipping copper DLC cold plates with early deployments meeting key thermal benchmarks. The article gives no test data, benchmark values or deployment numbers for these claims.
thermal: Copper cold plates with internal microchannels (180-micron microcapillaries and a gyroidal TPMS structure, per image captions) for high-density AI racks, with company-stated up to 10x lower pressure drop and operation on water around 44 °C.
manufacturing: Made by the Stack Forging process, which uses metal sheet lamination to produce single-piece copper plates with internal microfluidic channels without welds, brazing or seals; the internal design was shown by industrial CT scanning.

title: ZutaCore raises $100M to scale up waterless cooling for AI data centers
summary: ZutaCore Ltd. announced $100 million in Series C funding to scale deployments of its sealed, closed-loop, direct-to-chip two-phase cooling platform (HyperCool), which boils a dielectric fluid at the cold plate and uses no water. Per the article, the company says the system roughly halves cooling energy use against conventional setups, has logged more than 75 deployments across the Americas, Europe and Asia, and has built a 2-megawatt end-of-row emulation platform at its facility in Israel to test deployments before shipping. The named Series C investors are Mitsubishi Electric Corp., Carrier Ventures and Samsung Venture Investment Corp., with Goldman Sachs & Co. as exclusive placement agent. The performance and deployment figures are company statements, and the article reports no independent test results.
thermal: Sealed, closed-loop two-phase direct-to-chip cooling with a nonconductive dielectric fluid, targeting processors above 4,000 W and roughly halving cooling energy use (company claim), via the HyperCool platform and OmniTherm cold plate.
manufacturing: Tested on a 2-megawatt end-of-row emulation platform at ZutaCore's facility in Israel before customer shipment; the article gives no manufacturing details and no test results.

title: Using a Green Laser Facilitates 3D Printing of Pure Copper and Copper Alloys
summary: The article presents green-laser metal additive manufacturing machines (XH-M160G, M350G, M100G) from Chinese manufacturer Addireen for printing pure copper and copper alloys, based on Addireen's own material. Stated figures are 99.8% density, a minimum wall thickness of 0.08 mm, conductivity close to 100% IACS, thermal conductivity of approximately 390 W/m·K, and resistance to water pressures greater than 5 MPa, with print volumes from Ø100 x 100 mm to 350 x 350 x 500 mm. The article says the solutions are used in aerospace, energy, communications and transportation but names no customers or independent test organisations. These are supplier claims, and no test methods or independent verification are described.
thermal: Printed pure copper parts for heat transfer, including IGBT heat sink copper base plates, ultra-thin-wall heat dissipation fins (CuSn10) and induction heating coils, with stated thermal conductivity of approximately 390 W/m·K.
manufacturing: Laser powder-bed fusion using a high-power single-mode continuous fiber green laser; the article shows metallographic images of printed pure copper and says the parts withstand water pressure above 5 MPa, without giving a test method.

title: The Energy Store: F1's 2026 Battery Specifications Explained
summary: An explanatory article by Jarrod Partridge on the Energy Store, the battery in F1's 2026 hybrid power unit, and the regulatory limits that apply to it. It describes a 4MJ per-lap delta State of Charge limit, maximum charge and discharge power rates, and thermal management requirements, but gives no numerical values for the power rates, temperature limits or cooling performance. It says several manufacturers have developed dielectric fluid cooling systems for the Energy Store without naming any of them. The piece is editorial explanation rather than reporting of measured data.
thermal: Dielectric fluid cooling, with a non-conductive fluid circulated around or through the battery cell modules, is said to be used by several manufacturers, but the article gives no temperatures, flow rates or heat-load figures.
manufacturing: none: the article covers regulatory constraints, freedom of cell chemistry and pack form, and FIA Standard ECU battery management, with no build or test details for the Energy Store.

title: Integrated Air Cooling Oil Cooled System (ACOC), Periodic Reporting for period 2
publisher: CORDIS, Publications Office of the European Union
summary: HS Marston Aerospace (UK, coordinator) ran the H2020 ACOC project (grant 738160, 16 Jan 2017 to 15 Jan 2020) to develop an air-cooled oil cooler heat exchanger for Safran Helicopter Engines' TurboProp demonstrator. The page gives total cost '€ 949 988,75' and EU contribution '€ 664 276,38'. Three preliminary-design concepts (plate-fin baseline, laminate built from high-speed-machined layers, and additive manufacturing) were compared, and the laminate concept was chosen because the additive version could not finish detailed design and qualification in time. Six laminate ACOC units were manufactured; the page says the qualification tests were 'all passed first time' and the units 'have also run successfully' on the demonstrator, but no test data or performance numbers are given, so these are company claims. The page was last updated 6 Nov 2024.
thermal: Air-cooled oil cooler heat exchanger for an aero-engine, addressing rising thermal dissipation requirements in less available installation space.
manufacturing: Laminate heat exchanger built up layer by layer from high-speed-machined components; six units were manufactured after a manufacturing review and Critical Design Review, and additive manufacturing was assessed but not completed in time.

title: SW_INHEX (Innovative Heat Exchangers), Skywin labelled project, call 18
summary: Skywin's labelled-project page for SW_INHEX ('Innovative Heat Exchangers', call 18, R&D, total budget '4,5 M€') lists Safran Aero Boosters as leader, with Acte, Technochim and V2i as companies and Sirris, UCL and ULB as research bodies. The stated aim is to develop air/oil and air/gas heat exchangers in aluminium and Inconel using the Laser Beam Melting additive process, to make them lighter, more efficient and easier to adapt to the engine casing. The motivation given is that higher engine bypass ratios need greater oil cooling and preheating of air with heat recovered from exhaust gases. The page gives objectives and budget only, with no dates, results or test data, so this is a plan-stage project.
thermal: Air/oil and air/gas heat exchangers for aero-engine oil cooling and for preheating air using exhaust-gas heat recovery.
manufacturing: Additive manufacture of heat exchangers in aluminium and Inconel by Laser Beam Melting.

title: Breaking Ground in Sustainable Energy: Manufacturing Trials for Hydrogen Liquefaction Heat Exchanger Innovations (HLHX)
summary: Connected Places Catapult's Innovation Directory entry for the TRIG programme (shown as 'Year 2023', grant funded '£45,000') describes LUX Industries Ltd, an SME in the South East, working with subcontractor APEX, an additive manufacturing specialist, on heat exchanger manufacturing trials for LUX's hydrogen liquefaction system for airport ground support vehicles. The trials began with 316L stainless steel, producing a miniature heat exchanger that validated the core design and AM process, followed by a full-scale 316L heat exchanger. The conclusions say the work overcame challenges 'like powder removal and material porosity' and progressed 'from TRL 3 to TRL 4', but the page gives no thermal performance, leak-test or other numerical results, so these are company claims. Cryogenic testing is the next step toward TRL 5, and leak-test trials are described as part two of the project.
thermal: Heat exchanger for hydrogen liquefaction (cryogenic duty) in airport ground support systems; the page gives no thermal performance figures.
manufacturing: Full-scale 316L stainless steel heat exchanger additively manufactured by APEX within AM process limits, with powder removal and material porosity identified as challenges.

title: Development of additively manufactured cryogenic heat exchangers for hydrogen-electric aircraft propulsion
summary: Conference slides by Marco Vietze and Cenk Evrim of MT Aerospace for the German AdHyBau project (BMWK grant 20M1904B) on a printed heat exchanger that warms cryogenic hydrogen with a water-glycol loop in a hydrogen-electric aircraft drive. They built an analytical design tool for pin-fin tube-bundle cores, optimised for core mass with the hydrogen leaving above 290 K and under 1,000 Pa pressure drop in the core, and set the pin size and spacing limits from print trials in AlSi10Mg, 316L and Ti-6Al-4V. A full CFD model of about 126 million cells, using KIT's Ti-6Al-4V data, matched the tool's outlet temperatures within 3%, with total gas-side pressure drop under 2,000 Pa. The slides say the heat exchanger had been made and nitrogen cryogenic tests were being prepared; no test results are given.
thermal: Hydrogen to water-glycol heat exchanger that uses cryogenic hydrogen as the heat sink for an electric aircraft drive.
manufacturing: Laser powder-bed fused Ti-6Al-4V pin-fin core, with print trials setting minimum pin diameter and spacing.

title: Justification of the selection of a water-oil cooler when modernizing the cooling system of a diesel locomotive engine
summary: A 2026 paper proposes replacing two shell-and-tube oil-water coolers on a diesel locomotive's generator frame with a different water-oil cooler to improve the cooling system.
